What the platform does

01 / Overview

Etemad Melal is a Persian-language investment platform. Users create an account, verify a bank account, and top up their balance by bank transfer, uploading a receipt for confirmation.

From there, they choose one of five investment packages — each with its own ticket size, monthly return rate, and payout cap — and track their accrued profit as it builds toward that cap. Every deposit, withdrawal, and commission is logged in a filterable transaction history.

Behind the scenes, an admin panel gives staff an analytics dashboard, a referral tree for the platform's multi-level participation structure, financial reporting, and a support ticket system — all built on the same front end.

My role

02 / Contribution
  • →Built the full user-facing panel in Next.js and React, from authentication through package management, as the sole front-end developer on the project.
  • →Implemented multi-step forms with file upload and validation for bank account verification and balance top-ups.
  • →Built the package selection flow, letting users compare five investment tiers side by side before committing.
  • →Built a filterable, paginated transaction table covering deposits, withdrawals, and commissions.
  • →Implemented dark/light theme switching consistently across every screen in the panel.
  • →Built the admin side: role-based permissions, approval queues, and review workflows for financial and compliance operations.
  • →Contributed limited back-end work on supporting data endpoints alongside the front-end build.

Screens

03 / Walkthrough
Dashboard

Home — balance & active package

The landing screen after login: current balance, income breakdown, and the user's active investment package with a progress bar toward its payout cap.

Top-up

Charge account

Users transfer funds to a listed bank account, then submit the transaction reference and a receipt image for confirmation, with clear rules on what a valid receipt needs to show.

Withdraw

Withdrawal requests

A request form paired with a full history table, each row carrying a status badge — pending or approved — so users always know where their money is.

Bank accounts

Bank account verification

Users register an IBAN, card number, and account number for withdrawal, with a clear verified/unverified state on each saved account.

Packages

Buy a package

Five investment tiers shown side by side — ticket size, monthly return, payout cap, and contract length — as step one of a three-step purchase flow.

Packages

My packages

Active, reserved, and completed packages at a glance, with the active package's accrued profit tracked against its cap.

Transactions

Transaction history

Every deposit and withdrawal in one searchable, filterable table, with summary cards totaling pending withdrawals and completed deposits at the top.

Auth

Sign up & log in

Referral-code aware sign-up and a standard log-in screen, matching the panel's visual language from the very first touchpoint.

Admin panel & analytics

04 / Back office

Alongside the user-facing panel, staff get a separate back office: a full analytics dashboard, a visual referral tree, financial charts, and a support ticket system — plus a family of filterable report screens (commission ledger, purchase history, monthly payouts) built on one reusable stat-cards-and-table pattern.

Overview

Admin analytics dashboard

A year-by-year overview combining KPI cards, bar and line charts for purchase trends, and a package-by-package breakdown table — the main screen staff use to read the health of the platform at a glance.

Referral tree

Genealogy view

A node-based tree visualization mapping each user's referral network, color-coded by package status — a custom component built specifically for this multi-level structure.

Reporting

Financial dashboard

Gradient area and bar charts breaking down commissions by type and participation volume by branch, filterable by Persian calendar year.

Support

Support tickets

A filterable ticket list backing a threaded chat view, so staff and users can resolve account and withdrawal issues in one place.

Operations & governance

05 / Back office

Day-to-day operations run through the same panel: role-based permissions for staff, approval queues for pending deposits and withdrawals, and a full review workflow for insurance enrollment forms.

User management

Role-based permissions

Each staff account gets granular toggles — super admin, admin, support, accounting — controlling exactly what they can see and do across the panel.

Operations

Deposit & withdrawal approvals

A queue of pending transactions staff can approve or reject inline, with CSV export for offline reconciliation — the front line of the platform's financial operations.

Workflow

Insurance form review

A two-party review flow comparing policyholder and beneficiary details side by side, with status changes, reviewer notes, and PDF export — built as a small state machine from submission through approval.

Further back-office tools cover bank account verification, platform-wide announcements, scheduled events, and system configuration.
